newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Menem ready to accept justice minister resignation.
newsitem.headline: Menem ready to accept justice minister resignation.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem said Tuesday that he was ready to accept the resignation of Justice Minister Elias Jassan over contacts with a tycoon who is under police investigation in a murder case.
Menem told reporters in New York that despite the confirmation by government sources in Buenos Aires that Jassan had resigned, it was not official yet because he had not been informed.

"If minister Jassan resigns I will accept his resignation and name someone I have in mind," the Peronist leader told reporters. "But I have not spoken with him by phone at any moment, so for the time being he is still minister."

Government officials said earlier Tuesday that Jassan had offered Menem his resignation late Monday, after making what one official source called a "hardly convincing" defense of his conduct in a scandal involving Yabran.

Jassan, as well as Interior Minister Carlos Corach and Menem's Chief of Staff Alberto Kohan, have been accused by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo of manipulating the courts to protect Yabran's alleged criminal activities.

They have all denied the charges and Yabran denies any wrongdoing. But Jassan was caught lying a week ago when he first denied he knew Yabran, then had to admit to receiving more than 100 phone calls from the businessman's office.

Yabran, who has interests in strategic areas such as the private post and the airports, is accused by Cavallo and the political opposition of being the "head of the mafia," a charge which he angrily denied.

He has also been named by police as their "only lead" in investigations into who ordered the murder of photographer Jose Luis Cabezas in January. Cabezas, who took photos of Yabran for Noticias magazine, was shot and his body burnt.
